# GenUiDashboard

## Summary

A generative-UI analytics dashboard: a free-form canvas wall of linked cards where the AI answers questions by CREATING ChartCards and linking them in. Any card can live on the wall (`cards` is `linksToMany(CardDef)`) — ChartCards, Datasets, CRM records — each tile renders the linked card's embedded format, so a broken chart breaks only its own tile. Layout is Figma-style free placement: positions are pixel rects snapped to a 16px grid, persisted per-dashboard in `layoutJson` (keyed by the card id's last path segment so shipped example layouts survive a catalog install), with 8-direction drag-resize handles and one autosave on pointer release rather than per pointermove. Tiles move Figma-style: long-press anywhere on a tile (300ms) lifts it for dragging — quick clicks and presses on inner controls pass through — and every move, resize, or removal is undoable (⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z, or the on-canvas history buttons).

Data gets onto the wall three ways: (1) drop CSVs or images (screenshots, whiteboard photos) onto the canvas — CSVs parse locally via `parseCsv`, images go through a vision model; each file becomes its own Dataset card plus a suggested ChartCard, both linked here, with the original file written to the realm via `WriteBinaryFileCommand`; (2) type a live-web question — it goes to a search-grounded model (Perplexity Sonar) through `SendRequestViaProxyCommand`, and the cited answer lands as a Dataset (linked to its first source page) plus a ChartCard; (3) open the AI assistant with the bundled Gen UI Analyst skill via `UseAiAssistantCommand` and ask in natural language. Rows are capped to the 512KB realm card budget — never silently. A sun/moon toggle in the header switches the wall between its default Night Wall dark identity and a light scheme (ai-image-generator pattern: `data-theme` drives the themeless pin's variant; a linked theme takes over instead).

## Import

```js
import { GenUiDashboard } from '../gen-ui-dashboard';
```

## Usage

Create an instance and open it in interact mode — the isolated view IS the app. Fields:

- `title` — dashboard name
- `cards` — `linksToMany(CardDef)`: everything shown on the wall
- `layoutJson` — `{ [cardIdSlug]: { x, y, w, h } }`, managed by the canvas; you normally never edit it by hand

Drop a CSV on the canvas or click the live-web ask box to see a Dataset + ChartCard pair appear. Resize/data controls appear only on ChartCard tiles; other linked cards are just rendered.
